question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

In his celebrated poem, the poet compared life ___ a fleeting dream that vanishes with the dawn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When one thing is likened to another in a purely figurative or poetic sense — comparing two essentially different things — the preposition "to" is used. "Compare with" is reserved for examining the similarities and differences between two things of the same kind. Since the poet is likening life to a dream in a metaphor, the correct answer is "to".

◦ Complete sentence: In his celebrated poem, the poet compared life to a fleeting dream that vanishes with the dawn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "with" — this is used to examine the similarities and differences between two things of the same kind, not for a poetic or figurative likening.

 

• Option 3: "as" — "as" cannot follow "compared" in this construction.

 

• Option 4: "than" — "than" is used after a comparative adjective, not after "compared".

 

NOTE

 

• compared life to a dream, compared the heart to a pump (compare + to, for a figurative likening between different kinds of things); compare this year's sales with last year's (compare + with, to examine differences between things of the same kind).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The residents strongly objected (a)/ to build a new (b)/ shopping mall right (c)/ next to the park. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Object to" is a fixed expression in which "to" is a preposition, and a preposition must be followed by a gerund, not a base verb. So "objected to build" must be "objected to building".

◦ Corrected sentence: The residents strongly objected to building a new shopping mall right next to the park.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The residents strongly objected" is proper, with the adverb "strongly" modifying "objected".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "shopping mall right" is proper, with "right" used as an intensifier before "next to".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "next to the park." is proper, with "next to" showing position.

 

NOTE

 

• objected to paying the fine, objected to being ignored (object to + gerund), and not object to do.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

After moving to Norway for work, he quickly ___ the long, dark winters.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. got used to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Get used to" (= become accustomed to) is followed by a noun or gerund, and takes the appropriate tense of "get" to match the sentence. Since the sentence describes a completed past change, the correct form is the simple past "got used to". "Used to" alone (without "get / got") shows a past habit, and does not fit the sense of "becoming accustomed" intended here.

◦ Complete sentence: After moving to Norway for work, he quickly got used to the long, dark winters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "used to" — this shows a discontinued past habit ("he used to live there"), not the process of becoming accustomed to something.

 

• Option 2: "get used to" — the base form "get" does not agree with the past-tense context "quickly ___ the long, dark winters".

 

• Option 4: "getting used to" — the gerund form cannot stand alone as the main verb of the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• She got used to the noise of the city, They got used to waking up early (get / got used to + noun / gerund); He used to smoke (used to + base verb, for a discontinued habit).

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: The committee consists of five senior members.
option_2: The committee consists in five senior members.
option_3: The committee consists with five senior members.
option_4: The committee consists at five senior members.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The committee consists of five senior members.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Consist of" is used to show what a thing is made up of or composed of. Since the sentence describes the composition of the committee, the correct answer is "consists of five senior members".

◦ Correct sentence: The committee consists of five senior members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "consists in" — this is used to show what forms the essential or defining feature of something, not its composition, and does not fit here.

 

• Option 3: "consists with" — "with" is not the preposition used with "consist" in this sense.

 

• Option 4: "consists at" — "at" is not used with "consist" in this sense.

 

NOTE

 

• The committee consists of ten members, The syllabus consists of five units (consist + of, for composition); True happiness consists in contentment (consist + in, for an essential feature).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Mr. Verma, who joined the firm in 1998, is senior ___ all the other branch managers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Adjectives such as "senior", "junior", "superior", "inferior" and "prior" already carry a comparative sense and are followed by "to", never by "than". So the correct answer is "senior to".

◦ Complete sentence: Mr. Verma, who joined the firm in 1998, is senior to all the other branch managers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "than" — "than" follows a comparative adjective ending in "-er", such as "older than", and not "senior".

 

• Option 3: "from" — "from" is not the preposition used with "senior" in a comparison.

 

• Option 4: "over" — "over" does not fit this fixed comparative pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• He is junior to me by two years, Her qualifications are superior to his, this arrangement is prior to the merger (senior / junior / superior / inferior / prior + to), and not senior than.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Cycling to work is preferable (a)/ to sitting in traffic every morning (b)/ during the busy working week. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "Preferable" already carries a comparative sense and is followed by "to", never "than" — and it is correctly used here.

◦ Sentence as given: Cycling to work is preferable to sitting in traffic every morning during the busy working week.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Cycling to work is preferable" is proper, with the gerund "cycling" as the subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to sitting in traffic every morning" is proper, with "preferable to" correctly followed by a gerund.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "during the busy working week." is proper, with "during" followed by a noun phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Walking is preferable to driving in the city, a quiet evening at home is preferable to a noisy party (preferable + to), and not preferable than.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Having lived in the busy hostel for years, (a)/ he was fully accustomed (b)/ to share his room (c)/ with three other students. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Accustomed to" is a fixed expression in which "to" is a preposition, and a preposition must be followed by a gerund, not a base verb. So "accustomed to share" must be "accustomed to sharing".

◦ Corrected sentence: Having lived in the busy hostel for years, he was fully accustomed to sharing his room with three other students.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Having lived in the busy hostel for years," is proper, with the perfect participle "having lived" showing a completed action.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "he was fully accustomed" is proper, with the adverb "fully" modifying "accustomed".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "with three other students." is proper, with "with" showing accompaniment.

 

NOTE

 

• accustomed to waking up early, accustomed to eating spicy food (accustomed + to + gerund), and not accustomed to share.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The prolonged drought deprived the farmers ___ their entire harvest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "deprive someone of something", and not "deprive...from / off / with". So the correct answer is "of".

◦ Complete sentence: The prolonged drought deprived the farmers of their entire harvest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "from" — "from" is not the preposition used with "deprive".

 

• Option 2: "off" — "off" is a different word altogether and is never used with "deprive".

 

• Option 3: "with" — "with" does not fit the fixed expression "deprive...of".

 

NOTE

 

• deprived of sleep, deprived of basic rights (deprive + of), and not deprive from.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The old warehouse was found completely devoid from (a)/ any usable equipment (b)/ after the sudden factory closure. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "devoid of", and not "devoid from". So "devoid from" must be "devoid of".

◦ Corrected sentence: The old warehouse was found completely devoid of any usable equipment after the sudden factory closure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "any usable equipment" is proper, as the object of "of".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "after the sudden factory closure." is proper, with "after" showing sequence.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "devoid from" in part (a) is wrongly used where "devoid of" is needed.

 

NOTE

 

• devoid of emotion, devoid of any logic (devoid + of), and not devoid from.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Employees with over five years of continuous service (a)/ are eligible to a special loyalty bonus (b)/ during the festive season (c)/ announced by the management. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "eligible for", and not "eligible to". So "eligible to a special loyalty bonus" must be "eligible for a special loyalty bonus".

◦ Corrected sentence: Employees with over five years of continuous service are eligible for a special loyalty bonus during the festive season announced by the management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Employees with over five years of continuous service" is proper, with "with" introducing a descriptive phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "during the festive season" is proper, with "during" followed by a noun phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "announced by the management." is proper, with "by" showing the agent.

 

NOTE

 

• eligible for a scholarship, eligible for promotion (eligible + for), and not eligible to.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: She has been engaged to a research project for six months.
option_2: She has been engaged for a research project for six months.
option_3: She has been engaged in a research project for six months.
option_4: She has been engaged at a research project for six months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She has been engaged in a research project for six months.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Engaged in" is used to show that someone is occupied with an activity or task, while "engaged to" is used only for a forthcoming marriage. Since the sentence refers to a research project, the correct answer is "engaged in a research project".

◦ Correct sentence: She has been engaged in a research project for six months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "engaged to a research project" — "engaged to" is reserved for marriage, not for a task or activity.

 

• Option 2: "engaged for a research project" — "for" is not the preposition used with "engaged" in this sense.

 

• Option 4: "engaged at a research project" — "at" is not used with "engaged" in this sense.

 

NOTE

 

• engaged in social work, engaged in a heated debate (engaged + in, for an activity); engaged to be married, she is engaged to a doctor (engaged + to, for marriage).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Senior citizens above eighty years are exempt of (a)/ income tax (b)/ under the new government (c)/ scheme announced yesterday. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "exempt from", and not "exempt of". So "exempt of income tax" must be "exempt from income tax".

◦ Corrected sentence: Senior citizens above eighty years are exempt from income tax under the new government scheme announced yesterday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "income tax" is proper, as the object of "from".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "under the new government" is proper, with "under" showing the governing scheme.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "scheme announced yesterday." is proper, with the past participle "announced" describing the scheme.

 

NOTE

 

• exempt from duty, exempt from the examination fee (exempt + from), and not exempt of.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

I am truly grateful for my mentor for his constant patience during the difficult project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. grateful to my mentor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "grateful to" a person, and "grateful for" a thing. Since "my mentor" is a person, "grateful for my mentor" must be "grateful to my mentor".

◦ Corrected sentence: I am truly grateful to my mentor for his constant patience during the difficult project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "grateful of my mentor" — "of" is not the preposition used with "grateful".

 

• Option 3: "grateful with my mentor" — "with" is not used with "grateful" for a person.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "grateful for" cannot be used before a person.

 

NOTE

 

• grateful to my teacher, grateful to the doctor (grateful + to + person); grateful for your help, grateful for this opportunity (grateful + for + thing).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The jury found the defendant guilty of manslaughter (a)/ despite his lawyer's (b)/ passionate closing argument. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. The fixed expression is "guilty of" an offence, correctly used here.

◦ Sentence as given: The jury found the defendant guilty of manslaughter despite his lawyer's passionate closing argument.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The jury found the defendant guilty of manslaughter" is proper, with "guilty of" correctly followed by the offence.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "despite his lawyer's" is proper, with the possessive "'s" before "argument".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "passionate closing argument." is proper, with two adjectives before the noun.

 

NOTE

 

• guilty of theft, guilty of negligence (guilty + of), and not guilty for, guilty with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Despite repeated warnings, (a)/ the careless driver remained (b)/ indifferent for the safety rules (c)/ of the busy highway. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "indifferent to", and not "indifferent for". So "indifferent for the safety rules" must be "indifferent to the safety rules".

◦ Corrected sentence: Despite repeated warnings, the careless driver remained indifferent to the safety rules of the busy highway.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Despite repeated warnings," is proper, with "despite" followed directly by a noun phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the careless driver remained" is proper, with "remained" as a linking verb.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "of the busy highway." is proper, with "of" showing which rules.

 

NOTE

 

• indifferent to criticism, indifferent to public opinion (indifferent + to), and not indifferent for.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The young athlete has always been extremely keen for (a)/ representing the country (b)/ at the Olympics (c)/ ever since childhood. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "keen on", and not "keen for". So "keen for representing" must be "keen on representing".

◦ Corrected sentence: The young athlete has always been extremely keen on representing the country at the Olympics ever since childhood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "representing the country" is proper, with the gerund "representing" as the object of "on".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "at the Olympics" is proper, with "at" used before a specific event.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "ever since childhood." is proper, with "since" showing a point of time.

 

NOTE

 

• keen on cricket, keen on learning new skills (keen + on), and not keen for.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Under the terms of the new contract, the courier company is ___ any damage caused to fragile items during transit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. liable for.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Liable for" is used before a noun to show responsibility for a loss or damage, while "liable to" is used before a verb or an unpleasant consequence. Since "any damage" is a noun, the correct answer is "liable for".

◦ Complete sentence: Under the terms of the new contract, the courier company is liable for any damage caused to fragile items during transit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "liable on" — "on" is not the preposition used with "liable".

 

• Option 3: "liable with" — "with" is not used with "liable" in this sense.

 

• Option 4: "liable to" — this is used before a verb or an unpleasant consequence ("liable to fall ill"), not before a noun showing responsibility.

 

NOTE

 

• liable for the loss, held liable for the accident (liable + for + noun); liable to catch a cold, liable to be punished (liable + to + verb).

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: With regards to your query, we shall respond by Friday.
option_2: In regards of your query, we shall respond by Friday.
option_3: With regard to your query, we shall respond by Friday.
option_4: With reference of your query, we shall respond by Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. With regard to your query, we shall respond by Friday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct fixed phrase is "with regard to", using the singular "regard", and not the plural "regards". So the correct answer is "With regard to your query".

◦ Correct sentence: With regard to your query, we shall respond by Friday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "With regards to" — "regards" is wrongly used in the plural in this fixed phrase; only "regard" is standard here.

 

• Option 2: "In regards of" — this combines two errors: the plural "regards" and the wrong preposition "of".

 

• Option 4: "With reference of" — the correct phrase is "with reference to", and not "with reference of".

 

NOTE

 

• with regard to the matter, with reference to your letter (with regard / reference + to), and not with regards to, with reference of.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The refund for the cancelled order was processed ___ the company's standard policy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. in accordance with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed phrase is "in accordance with", and not "in accordance to / of" or "in according with". So the correct answer is "in accordance with".

◦ Complete sentence: The refund for the cancelled order was processed in accordance with the company's standard policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "in accordance to" — "to" is not the preposition used in this fixed phrase.

 

• Option 2: "in accordance of" — "of" is not used in this fixed phrase.

 

• Option 3: "in according with" — the noun form "accordance" is required after "in", not the verb form "according".

 

NOTE

 

• in accordance with the rules, in accordance with the agreement (in accordance + with), and not in accordance to, according with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

All the new recruits were subjected with (a)/ a thorough background check (b)/ before being issued (c)/ their official identity cards. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "subjected to", and not "subjected with". So "subjected with a thorough background check" must be "subjected to a thorough background check".

◦ Corrected sentence: All the new recruits were subjected to a thorough background check before being issued their official identity cards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a thorough background check" is proper, as the object of "to".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "before being issued" is proper, with the passive gerund "being issued".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "their official identity cards." is proper, with the possessive "their" agreeing with "recruits".

 

NOTE

 

• subjected to harsh criticism, subjected to a series of tests (subjected + to), and not subjected with.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The shopkeeper grew jealous (a)/ about his rival's growing (b)/ popularity in the neighbourhood. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression for envy directed at another person's success is "jealous of", and not "jealous about". So "jealous about his rival's growing popularity" must be "jealous of his rival's growing popularity".

◦ Corrected sentence: The shopkeeper grew jealous of his rival's growing popularity in the neighbourhood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The shopkeeper grew jealous" is proper, with "grew" as a linking verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "popularity in the neighbourhood." is proper, with "in" showing location.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "jealous about" in part (b) is wrongly used where "jealous of" is needed.

 

NOTE

 

• jealous of his success, jealous of her achievements (jealous + of, for envy of another's success), and not jealous about someone else's achievement.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The charity's tireless work (a)/ over the past decade (b)/ has made it thoroughly worthy for (c)/ national recognition. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

• The fixed expression is "worthy of", and not "worthy for". So "worthy for national recognition" must be "worthy of national recognition".

◦ Corrected sentence: The charity's tireless work over the past decade has made it thoroughly worthy of national recognition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The charity's tireless work" is proper, with the possessive "'s" before "tireless work".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "over the past decade" is proper, with "over" showing a duration.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "national recognition." is proper, as the object of "of".

• worthy of praise, worthy of respect (worthy + of), and not worthy for.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The manager promised to ___ the customer's complaint immediately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. look into.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Look into" means "to investigate", which fits the context of examining a complaint. "Look after" means "to take care of", "look for" means "to search for", and "look on" means "to watch passively" — none of these fit the sense of investigating a complaint.

◦ Complete sentence: The manager promised to look into the customer's complaint immediately.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "look after" — this means "to take care of", which does not fit a complaint that needs investigation.

 

• Option 2: "look for" — this means "to search for", which does not fit an existing complaint.

 

• Option 3: "look on" — this means "to watch without taking part", which does not fit the sense of investigating.

 

NOTE

 

• look into the matter, look into the allegations (look into = investigate); look after the children (take care of); look for the missing file (search for).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

All the candidates who registered online will sit in (a)/ the entrance examination (b)/ at the designated centres (c)/ next Sunday morning. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression for taking an examination is "sit for", and not "sit in". So "will sit in the entrance examination" must be "will sit for the entrance examination".

◦ Corrected sentence: All the candidates who registered online will sit for the entrance examination at the designated centres next Sunday morning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the entrance examination" is proper, as the object of "for".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "at the designated centres" is proper, with "at" showing location.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "next Sunday morning." is proper, with no preposition needed before "next".

 

NOTE

 

• sit for the board exams, sit for an interview (sit + for, for taking a test), and not sit in an exam.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

After finishing school, she decided to ___ Oxford University for a scholarship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. apply to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Apply to" is used before the name of an institution, while "apply for" is used before the thing being sought, such as a job or a scholarship. Since "Oxford University" is an institution, the correct answer is "apply to".

◦ Complete sentence: After finishing school, she decided to apply to Oxford University for a scholarship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "apply for" — this is used before the thing being sought, such as "apply for a scholarship", not before an institution.

 

• Option 3: "apply at" — "at" is not the standard preposition before the name of an institution in this sense.

 

• Option 4: "apply in" — "in" is not used with "apply" before an institution.

 

NOTE

 

• apply to Harvard for admission, apply to the bank for a loan (apply + to + institution); apply for a job, apply for a visa (apply + for + thing sought).
